DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The clinical presentation of double vision (diplopia), proximal muscle weakness (difficulty climbing stairs, upper limb weakness), and the confirmed presence of Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies are diagnostic of Myasthenia Gravis. The normal Chest CT rules out a thymoma, a common associated tumor, though it may still be present. The muscle fatigue you described is consistent with this condition, which worsens with activity and improves with rest. Have you noticed that your symptoms tend to get worse later in the day or after physical exertion?
